dek: SportsCapPro sells rated picks with a written analysis, through its own site and through CapperTek, where a pass ran from $15 for a day to $325 for 60 days. The only full record we could open, its CapperTek log, shows 118-143-2 and -93.01 units from Feb 2025 to Feb 2026.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded SportsCapPro. The record below is CapperTek's log, which we read but did not audit. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: SportsCapPro is a small pick service covering the NFL, NBA, college football and basketball, and baseball. Each play is rated 1 to 4 and, it says, comes with a written explanation. Its own site showed us a human check on 7 Nov 2026 instead of content, so this review relies on its CapperTek listing, where it pays to be a Pro Featured service, and on Wayback Machine copies of its site from May 2025.

The record is the main finding. CapperTek's log, with a time stamp on every pick, shows 261 graded picks from 20 Feb 2025 to 25 Feb 2026 at 118-143-2, 45% winners, -93.01 units and an ROI of -4.77%. The last 365 days alone were 16-29. Nothing had been logged there in the 255 days before our check.

Customer reviews are few and all sit on CapperTek: four long positive reviews posted between 28 Feb and 8 Mar 2025, and a complaint about a $149 purchase with no picks that the same buyer withdrew the next day. The positive reviews describe winning seasons that the CapperTek log does not show, though that log may not hold every play sent to subscribers.
pricing_intro: SportsCapPro's own site did not open for us on 7 Nov 2026. Current prices below come from its CapperTek pass page that day. Prices from its own site come from Wayback Machine copies dated 18 May 2025 and may have changed.

Archived page: if not in profit when it expires, an additional year free
MLB and NBA playoff special (archived May 2025)

Baseball, basketball, college, NFL and combination packages listed; prices not captured

guarantee: The archived All Sports page, as saved on 18 May 2025, said that a buyer who had "not shown a PROFIT" when the yearly subscription expired would get another full year free, and that the same applied to full season and combination packages. That is more picks, not money back, and it does not cover losses on the bets.
We saw no guarantee on the current CapperTek pass page, and CapperTek's terms say fees are non refundable unless stated otherwise. We could not read SportsCapPro's own current terms.

claims_note: The archived site's four testimonials, signed with a first name and a town, were chosen by the seller. The CapperTek reviewers describe seasons around 55% to 58% and a 39-21 March Madness run in 2023, two years before the CapperTek log begins, so we could not check them.

Units do not line up. The bio and one reviewer describe a 1 to 4 unit scale, while the CapperTek log mostly shows stakes of 6 and 11 units. We do not know how the two scales map, so judge the log by win rate and ROI rather than raw units.
record: What is independently verifiable: CapperTek, not SportsCapPro, keeps its pick log. The all time history we opened on 7 Nov 2026 listed 261 graded picks from 20 Feb 2025 to 25 Feb 2026, mostly college basketball (166) and baseball (73). Each entry showed the game start time, the time the pick was made and the time it was graded, and every pick was made before the listed start. CapperTek's totals: 118-143-2, 45% winners, -93.01 units, ROI -4.77%. The last 365 days alone: 16-29, -85.53 units, ROI -27.45%.

Limits of that log: CapperTek is paid by featured sellers, so it is not a neutral auditor. We could not see voided picks, and subscribers on SportsCapPro's own site may get plays that are never posted on CapperTek. With nothing logged after 25 Feb 2026, football barely appears (3 college football picks and 1 NFL pick).

What is the seller's own marketing: the testimonials and "Consistent Winning Record" language on the archived site, and blog posts grading single days. We found no full record on SportsCapPro's own site, which we could not open today, and our web searches found no court or regulator action naming SportsCapPro.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition SportsCapPro is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about its picks beyond the CapperTek log described above.
our_data.context: For scale: SportsCapPro's reviewers describe seasons in the mid to high 50s by win rate, while its CapperTek log sits at 45%. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Every independent buyer review we found sits on CapperTek, a site SportsCapPro pays for featured placement and where it replies to reviews. There are six posts from five accounts, all from 2025, and the four positive ones arrived within 16 days of its first CapperTek pick on 20 Feb 2025. We found no Trustpilot page, no SmartCustomer reviews and no Reddit or forum thread.

customers.text: A reviewer said following SportsCapPro brought significant profits and praised its clear, well researched analysis, especially in tournaments. No record or amount was given. SportsCapPro replied that the reviewer had joined a couple of years earlier.

A reviewer said he started with a one week package in Nov 2021 on a friend's tip, later moved to the yearly All Sports package, and has had no losing season overall in baseball, football or basketball since. He liked the small number of plays and the explanation with each one.
A reviewer who said he had lost with about six services over 20 years claimed a profit every season in each major sport over three years with SportsCapPro, betting its suggested unit sizes.

A reviewer said he joined in Feb 2023 on a friend's recommendation, that the March Madness package went 39-21, and that the service hits around 55% to 58% most seasons. Those figures are his and fall before the CapperTek log begins.
A buyer said he paid $149, never received a pick, and got no reply to calls, texts or emails, calling it "just another scam."
The next day the same buyer posted that SportsCapPro had finally responded and "made it right," and that he was withdrawing his complaint. He did not say what was done.
The site's homepage showed four testimonials signed with a first name and a town, praising steady bankroll growth, the analysis with each pick and NFL results. The seller chose and published them.
SmartCustomer showed 0 reviews for sportscappro.com, Trustpilot returned no page for it, and our searches found no Reddit, TheRX, SBR or Covers forum thread about SportsCapPro.

conflicts: SportsCapPro is a Pro Featured Verified service on CapperTek, and CapperTek's FAQ says featured services pay a monthly advertising fee. Its customer reviews are hosted on that same site, where SportsCapPro replies to them.
We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the archived SportsCapPro pages or on its CapperTek profile. We could not check its current site.
strengths: A time stamped log kept by an outside site, with every pick made before the start, is more than many sellers offer.
Each play carries a rating, and many logged picks include a written explanation, so a buyer can judge the reasoning.
A $15 one day pass on CapperTek allows a cheap test.
A complaint about a missing purchase was resolved, according to the buyer's own follow up.
concerns: The only full record we could open shows a loss: 118-143-2 and -93.01 units over 261 picks, and 16-29 in the last 365 days.
No picks had been posted on CapperTek since 25 Feb 2026, so current activity there is unclear.
The site advertised a "Consistent Winning Record" and "trackable results" that we could not find.
Reviews are few, arrived in a cluster, and sit on a site the service pays.
The guarantee we saw was an extra year of picks, not money back, and no owner or company is named.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It appears to be a real, small service: it has sold passes on CapperTek since early 2025, logged 261 time stamped picks there, and one buyer said a missed delivery was put right. We could not open its own site or find a named owner or company.
On CapperTek on 7 Nov 2026 a pass cost $15 for a day, $90 for 7 days, $210 for 30 days or $325 for 60 days. An archived copy of its site from May 2025 listed the All Sports package at $699 a year.
Does SportsCapPro have a verified record?

The closest thing is its CapperTek log, which time stamps every pick and showed 118-143-2 and -93.01 units from Feb 2025 to Feb 2026. CapperTek is paid by featured sellers, and Watchdog has not graded SportsCapPro itself.

You get a small number of rated plays with written analysis and a cheap one day pass to try it. What is unproven, and not supported by the only log we could open, is that the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110; that log was at 45% winners.
